deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a fair copy of notes from a history course or textbook on ancient Greek history, continuing from the previous page (Pericles, the Thirty Years' Peace, the Corcyra affair). The heading reads 'Lage von Griechenland, vor diesem Kriege' ('The situation of Greece before this war', meaning the Peloponnesian War). The content, step by step:

(1) Athens and Sparta are now the two leading states, but their power differs in kind: Athens is strong by its fleet, Sparta by its land forces.

(2) Athens leads the allied Greeks (the Delian League), although there has long been great discontent with Athenian rule.

(3) Sparta can present itself as the liberator of Greece. The discontented join Sparta because its allies pay no tribute.

(4) Pericles ran a brilliant administration and for a long time rendered no accounts. Yet it was apparently not wasteful ('nicht so verschwenderisch'): a treasure of 1,000,000 (or possibly 7,000,000) Reichsthaler was found.

(5) Spartan envoys demand that Athens give up its claim to hegemony over Greece. Athens refuses, and in 431 the '27-year war' breaks out.

(6) Almost all Greek states take part. On the Athenian side are all the islands of the Archipelago except Thera and Melos, the islands off western Greece, and the Greek [cities ...]. The list continues on the next page.

The hand and the content (a schoolroom or lecture outline in Weltgeschichte) suggest a student notebook bound into the Nachlass, not Gauss's own mathematical work. Nothing mathematical is being computed. The only numbers are dates and quantities: the year 431, the 27-year duration, and the treasury figure.
errors: Historical content is essentially accurate for a textbook summary. Thucydides (2.9) indeed names Melos and Thera as the only Cycladic islands not on the Athenian side. The war's outbreak in 431 BC and its 27-year length (431–404 BC) are correct.

The treasury figure '1000000 rl' (Reichsthaler) is a modernized and probably garbled conversion. Thucydides 2.13 gives 6000 talents of coined silver on the Acropolis, which under early-19th-c. conversions (roughly 1000–1500 Thaler per talent) would be several million Thaler, not one million. The first digit may actually be a 7, which would fit better.
Characterizing the Spartan allies as joining 'because they paid no tribute' is a simplification, but a standard one in period textbooks.

results.what: Narrative summary of the causes and alignments at the outbreak of the Peloponnesian War (431 BC), after Thucydides
results.modern_name: Ancient Greek history: the Peloponnesian War (Thucydides, Book 2)
results.usually_credited_to: Thucydides; 18th/19th-c. German history textbooks (e.g. Heeren, Becker)

deep.surprise_reason: Non-mathematical school or lecture notes on Greek history, probably in a student's hand (perhaps a family member's notebook bound into the bundle). There is no mathematical content to attribute to Gauss.

checkable.asserts: The Peloponnesian War, 431–404 BC, lasted 27 years, matching '27 jährige Krieg'.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Athen war mächtig [?] durch seine Flotten' — the illegible bit likely reads 'mächtig, (haupt)sächlich durch seine Flotten' or simply 'mächtig durch'; the sense is unchanged.
Lines 11–12: 'aber gleichwohl war sie nicht schw[?] [?]' should read approximately 'aber gleichwohl war sie nicht so verschwenderisch, es fand sich ein Schatz von ...'.
Treasury figure: the first digit of '1000000 rl.' is uncertain and may be '7' ('7000000 rl.').

Last lines: 'ausgenommen Thera, und Melos die Inseln an der Westseite' should be read as 'ausgenommen Thera und Melos; die Inseln an der Westseite von Griechenland, die griechischen [Städte ...]' (punctuation of the list).
